title: Malformed Iam refusal
issueTitle: Handshake parsing accepts an empty peer name on extra whitespace
function: The `webtools-udp` server trims an unframed handshake line and splits it on a single space, so `Iam  x` registered a peer named `""` and a bare `Iam` died in a stack-trace WARN. This plan makes the server refuse every malformed `Iam` line with `REFUSED malformed`, from any origin, before `admit` and without touching a registration, and moves the KDoc, tests and living documents that said otherwise. A contained bugfix in one module, shipped as `webtools-udp` `2.0.0a`.

gap.summary: `parseHandshake` is `runCatching { require(verb); require(size >= 2); Handshake(tokens[1], tokens.getOrElse(2) { "" }) }`: `Iam  x` parses to a handshake named `""`, `Iam bob  tok` to one indistinguishable from `Iam bob`, and a bare `Iam` is a `Result.failure` carrying a stack trace. Absent and present-but-empty slots are conflated, and the handshake's only throw path sits here.
gap.detail: The split on a single U+0020 keeps consecutive empty strings, so a run of spaces produces an empty slot. `Result` is the module's type for operational failures; its domain outcomes (`Admission`, `SendOutcome`, `ReceiveOutcome`, `OfferResult`) are sealed types.
evidence: research/malformed-line-handling.md §3.2, §5.A — the sealed-outcome finding and the totality argument

options.name: A sealed `HandshakeParse` outcome with a `HandshakeDefect` enum
options.summary: A total `parseHandshake(tokens): HandshakeParse` with three arms, `NotAHandshake`, `Malformed(defect)` and `Valid(handshake)`; the credential slot read with `getOrNull`, so absent (`null`, carried as `""`) and present-but-empty (malformed) are told apart.
options.why: Fits the module's idiom for domain outcomes, gives the coordinator a compiler-checked exhaustive `when`, carries the defect for the log, and allocates no exception on the path a hostile sender drives. KEEP-0127 reserves `Result` for generic failures.

options.name: Keep `Result<Handshake>` and treat every post-recognition failure as malformed
options.why: `runCatching` catches every `Throwable`, so an unrelated bug inside the parse would be answered `REFUSED malformed` instead of surfacing; it carries no defect for the log; it builds a stack-trace-bearing exception per hostile datagram.
options.wins: Only if zero churn in the two existing parse tests mattered more than those points.

options.name: A typed `MalformedHandshakeException` inside `Result`
options.why: The stack-trace cost stays and exhaustiveness is lost: the coordinator would need `exceptionOrNull() as?` plus an `else` for failures it does not know.
options.wins: If the project paradigm forbade sealed outcomes, which it does not (`Admission`, `SendOutcome`).

options.name: A separate validity check before parsing
options.why: Two copies of the slot logic, a `Result` that can no longer fail, and a check a caller can forget.

options.name: Split on `\s+`, the issue's second proposal
options.why: Redefines the wire format and silently turns `Iam bob  tok` into a different valid line. The single-U+0020 split is the contract.

options.name: A `String?` credential or a `Credential` sum type in `Handshake`
options.why: The only consumer maps it straight back to `String` for `admit`, and `""` inside a `Handshake` is unambiguous once the slot read rejects present-but-empty.

verdict.summary: `HandshakeProtocol` gains a sealed `HandshakeParse`, a three-entry `HandshakeDefect` enum with fixed log-safe labels, a total `parseHandshake` that checks the verb through `isHandshake`, then the name, then the credential, and `MALFORMED_REFUSAL_DATAGRAM` built once beside `REGISTERED_DATAGRAM`. `Handshake`, `isHandshake` and `extraTokenCount` keep their signatures; `MIN_TOKENS` goes.
verdict.defense: One definition of recognition (`isHandshake` feeds the `NotAHandshake` arm), one definition of validity, no throw path left in the handshake, and the name slot checked before the credential slot so `Iam  x y` reports the name defect. The sealed type is closed on purpose: the routing's exhaustive `when` is what guarantees that a future arm, such as #53's, is routed.

gap.summary: `classify` splits the trimmed text twice (`isHandshake(text.split(' ')) -> handleHandshake(origin, text.split(' '))`) and `handleHandshake` parses first and routes a `Result`: a bare `Iam` ends in the listener's stack-trace WARN with no reply; `Iam  x` and `Iam bob  tok` get `REGISTERED 2` from a registered origin and reach `admit` from an unknown one, registering the name `""`.
gap.detail: An exception anywhere inside `accept` ends the `mcups-listener` thread (`flatMap` is a plain `fold`; `receiveLoop` has no `try`), so every new path has to be exception-free. The liveness stamp for a registered origin runs before classification and is out of scope.
evidence: main/HandshakeCoordinator.kt:220-232 — the `null`-tag branch; two splits at :227
main/HandshakeCoordinator.kt:243-293 — `handleHandshake`: parse, extra-token DEBUG, `findByOrigin`, `admit`, supersede, register
main/MultiConnectionUDPServer.kt:326-340 — `receiveLoop` logs a `Result.failure` with the exception at :336

options.name: One split, one parse, an exhaustive `when` that routes four ways
options.summary: `NotAHandshake` → today's "sender may be pre-2.0" WARN; `Malformed` → one WARN and `REFUSED malformed` to any origin, returning the send's `Result`; `Valid` → the extra-token DEBUG, then today's registered-origin retransmit or the untouched `admit`, supersede, register path.
options.why: One token list per hostile datagram instead of two, no exception allocation, and the compiler checks that every outcome is routed. The malformed arm returns the send's `Result` exactly as the `admit` refusal does, so the listener adds no stack-trace WARN.

options.name: Silence, or `REGISTERED 2`, for a registered origin's malformed line
options.summary: What the research recommended, following DTLS, WireGuard and ENet, which discard a bad first message silently.
options.why: The registered peer and the unknown peer would follow different rules for the same bytes, and `REGISTERED 2` would answer an accept to a line the server defines as malformed. One reply for every malformed line keeps the rule one sentence; the reflection and client-WARN costs are stated in the protocol doc.
options.wins: If a strict 3x anti-amplification bound were adopted as a module requirement; it is not.
options.source: architecture.md §9; research/README.md § Where the findings differ

options.name: Keep `isHandshake` as the gate in `classify` and a `require` on the verb inside `parseHandshake`
options.why: An exception inside `accept` ends the listener thread; a total parse with a `NotAHandshake` arm costs one `when` arm and removes the only throw path.
options.wins: Only once #54's guard existed, and even then the arm is cheaper.

verdict.summary: `classify`'s `null` branch splits once and calls a new `routeUnframed`, an exhaustive `when` over `HandshakeParse`. `refuseMalformed` handles the malformed arm with one WARN (`Refusing malformed handshake from {} ({}); origin registered: {}`: the origin, the defect label, the flag) and `send(MALFORMED_REFUSAL_DATAGRAM, origin)`. `handleHandshake` keeps the valid line's lookup and retransmit; `admitAndRegister` is today's body moved verbatim, #49 ordering included.
verdict.defense: The malformed arm never reaches `admit`, never looks up by name, never supersedes, registers nothing and fires no `onRegistered`; its registration lookup is read-only, for the log field. The WARN never carries the line, its tokens, the name or the credential, and attaches no exception (CWE-117; the OWASP logging guidance). `accept`'s `@return` narrows to: failure only when a reply could not be delivered or `admit` threw.

gap.summary: No reply exists for a malformed line: a bare `Iam` draws nothing and the empty-slot shapes draw an accept. The one reply builder, `HandshakeWireFormat.refusedMessage`, trims and collapses its reason and compiles a `Regex` on every call, the wrong cost on a path the sender paces.
evidence: main/HandshakeWireFormat.kt:117-120 — `refusedMessage` compiles a `Regex` per call at :118
research/refusal-reply-text.md §6.1, §7 — the text and the amplification arithmetic

options.name: `REFUSED malformed`: one fixed reason, bytes built once
options.summary: 17 bytes, the same for all three shapes, built once through `refusedMessage("malformed")` into an `internal val` beside `REGISTERED_DATAGRAM`; the defect goes to the server log only.
options.why: A hand-rolled client's author needs a cause; one reason for three shapes gives a prober no oracle; precomputing avoids a `Regex` per hostile datagram. Payload ratio 5.7 on the 3-byte trigger (1.45 on the wire), in the range `admit` refusals already produce: the README's own `invalid credential` example is 5.2.

options.name: `REFUSED malformed handshake`
options.why: Repeats "handshake" inside the client's own exception message ("Server refused the handshake: …") and gives the 3-byte trigger a ratio of 9.

options.name: A reason that names the slot
options.why: Three replies instead of one, longer, and an oracle for a prober.

options.name: A bare `REFUSED`
options.why: Leaves the hand-rolled-client author, who is exactly who sends a malformed line, with no cause; SMTP likewise advises against bare codes.

options.name: A parameterised or configurable reason text
options.why: The reason is informative wire text a third-party client must not branch on, and an application's `admit` may return the same word; making it configurable invites the branching the protocol doc warns against.

verdict.summary: `MALFORMED_REFUSAL_DATAGRAM`, an `internal val ByteArray` on `HandshakeProtocol`, built once from `HandshakeWireFormat.refusedMessage("malformed")`; the reason string is a `private const val`. `HandshakeWireFormat` itself is not edited in code.
verdict.defense: The reply verb and its handling are already Stable Core (`REFUSED_REPLY`, `isRefused`, `refusalReason`); only the reason text is new and it sits outside the contract, so no consumer can build on it. The shared array is read-only, like `REGISTERED_DATAGRAM`.

gap.summary: The class and `admit` KDoc of `MultiConnectionUDPServer` and the `REFUSED` section of `HandshakeWireFormat` say that `REFUSED` comes only from `admit` and that the default admits every well-formed `Iam`. After the fix both sentences are false, and `admit`'s input domain (never an empty name; credential `""` only when absent) is stated nowhere.

options.name: Restate both KDocs: refused before `admit`, whatever the origin's state; `admit` never sees an empty name
options.why: Documents enforced behaviour; it narrows `admit`'s input domain and is additive for every existing override. Stable Core wording, no signature change. No alternative was weighed: a reader of the public API must not learn the rule from the protocol doc alone.

verdict.summary: KDoc only, no code: `MultiConnectionUDPServer` (class KDoc, `admit`) and `HandshakeWireFormat` (the `REFUSED` reply section, `REFUSED_REPLY`) state that a malformed `Iam` is refused `REFUSED malformed` before `admit` and whatever the origin's state, that `admit` never sees an empty `name` and sees `credential` as `""` only when absent, and that the reason text is informative.
verdict.defense: The `admit` KDoc is where an implementer of a server looks; the protocol doc is where a client author looks. Both must say the same thing.

steps.what: `HandshakeProtocolTest`: a tab inside a name is still `Valid`, known gap tracked as #53.

asBuilt.summary: Left as planned: the 4a test `parseHandshake accepts non-space whitespace inside a name - known gap tracked as 53` pins it, protocol doc §3 links #53, and a comment on #53 records that it inherits this change's rule.
asBuilt.verified: The pinning test passes on the final tree.

gap.summary: `handshakeMessage("")` builds `Iam ` unvalidated and `MultiConnectionUDPClient.handshake` sends it inside `runCatching`; a library client can still put a malformed line on the wire and learns of it only from the server.

options.name: Leave the client to #52; test the new server branch from raw sockets
options.why: #52 owns the client; once it lands the library client cannot send a malformed line, which is why every socket-level test of the new branch sends from a `DatagramSocket`.

options.name: Add the client-side checks in this change
options.why: The issue is the server's rule; #52 is filed and its design will settle both the message builder and `handshake()`.

verdict.summary: Not changed. A library client with an empty name now fails fast with `HandshakeRefusedException`, reason `malformed`; #52 will move that failure local.
verdict.defense: The protocol doc lists the library-client calls that send a malformed line, so the behaviour is documented until #52 removes it.

asBuilt.summary: Left as planned, and pinned harder than planned: the first review added the 4b e2e test that fails fast with a typed `malformed` refusal and flips when #52 lands.

changes.what: The 4b e2e test `a nameless handshake fails fast with a typed malformed refusal and registers nothing`.
changes.why: Maintainer decision at the first review.

followUps.note: Client-side handshake validation. Makes the library client unable to send a malformed line; why the socket-level tests here use a raw socket. The 4b test pins today's behaviour and flips when #52 lands.

Non-space whitespace in names and credentials. Adds `HandshakeDefect` entries and checks inside `parseHandshake`, and replaces the protocol doc's known-gap paragraph. Inherits the rule that every malformed line is refused whatever its origin.
A throwing `onClientConnect` ends the listener thread. Orthogonal: this change adds no throw path; #54's guard lands in `receiveLoop` and around `onRegistered`.
Rate-bounding the per-datagram WARN logs. Covers the new malformed WARN and the client's unframed-drop WARN for a reflected `REFUSED`; the fixed template and defect label are its key.
Registration orphaned when the `REGISTERED` send fails. Its fix lands inside the moved, unchanged admit-and-register path, now marked `FIXME(#49)`.
A registered origin's `Iam` gets `REGISTERED 2` even when it names a different client. Pre-existing and unchanged; the protocol doc states it.
Replies to unverified source addresses, with no rate limit. Unchanged by this fix, which adds one more reply (17 bytes) to the set; the protocol doc advises edge rate limiting.
